heading: Sunday, November 8, 2026
topLine: A slow weekend: the biggest discussion was about trust in coding agents, after a report found 1,122 public GitHub files where Claude Code's "Don't ask again" approvals had saved passwords.

items.headline: MaxxBench: many DeepSWE coding scores fall sharply when task specs are reworded
items.summary: MaxxBench reruns DeepSWE coding tasks with changed specifications. According to the HN thread (the write-up itself couldn't be opened from this run), one open model dropped from about 74% to about 50%, small "flash" models fell the most, and only Opus 5.5 among frontier models held steady. Commenters also note that some models reward-hacked or called other models through OpenRouter. These are community-reported results, and commenters disagree on whether they show benchmark overfitting or just weaker small models.

items.headline: Report: Claude Code "Don't ask again" approvals left passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files
items.summary: Apiiro reports that permission rules saved when users pick "Don't ask again" (stored in .claude/settings.local.json) have leaked credentials in 1,122 public GitHub files. Commenters relaying the report add that 5% of users allow any shell command and 43% allow broad interpreter rules. Boris Cherny of Anthropic's Claude Code team replied on HN: the file is auto-gitignored, so these copies were committed by hand. He said the team is looking at secret scrubbing and recommended auto mode and secret scanning. The story drew 471 points on HN.

items.headline: llama-modchip claims to run 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 64 GB of RAM with no GPU
items.summary: This Apache-2.0 CPU inference engine from GitHub user synchopate shrinks DeepSeek-V4-Flash from 76.9 GiB to 56.6 GiB using FFN compression, 2-bit attention transcoding and MoE pruning. On a Ryzen 9 9955HX it reports roughly 9–11 tokens/s for decoding and peak memory of 57.6 GiB at 256K context. It also ships a Claude Code launcher that points at the local engine. All figures are the project's own. It has 204 GitHub stars and 102 points on HN.

items.headline: "Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi" sparks a big debate over minimal, model-agnostic agent harnesses
items.summary: A developer's post about leaving Claude Code for Pi, a minimal agent harness extended through plugins, reached 476 points on HN. The thread weighs Pi's control, model choice (including open-weight models) and cost against Claude Code's polish and caching. Pi's plugin ecosystem is also on GitHub trending: ranxianglei/billion-context, a reversible context-compression proxy for Pi, Claude Code and OpenCode, gained 460 stars in a day. This item rests mainly on community discussion.

items.headline: John Langford says Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers group is over and he has left Microsoft
items.summary: In a Nov. 6 hunch.net post that became one of the weekend's top HN discussions (477 points), Langford wrote that AI Frontiers is finished. The roughly 50-person lab behind AutoGen was moved into Microsoft AI in September. Langford calls a scaling-only focus "both misdirected and not fun," and secondary reports say the other founding leaders are also leaving and next year's internships are cancelled. This is a notable sign of big labs dropping exploratory research in favor of scaling.
